2610.10478.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
2610.10478.paper_summary: How can we predict which base checkpoint is worth an expensive round of agentic post-training? End-to-end pass@$K$ tests whether successful behavior already appears in a base model's distribution, but it is a poor fit for agentic coding: many base checkpoints cannot reliably produce the well-formed tool invocation required to complete a task end-to-end. Single-shot or short-horizon tasks avoid these tool-calling failures by collapsing a multi-step interaction into a fixed prompt and a single patch, but they sidestep the core capability we care about: maintaining coherent state over many tool-using steps as the repository evolves. To bridge this gap, we treat successful post-trained agent trajectories as a lookahead signal of base-model potential. Replaying each trajectory and rerunning tests after every code-changing step identifies the decisive step: the first step whose cumulative patch flips the repository from failing to passing, certifying that the recorded action solves the task given the prior context. Motivated by a coverage principle for agentic traces, we build three screens at this step that do not require a base checkpoint to drive the harness from a cold start: (i) Decisive-Action BPB (bits per byte) measures the probability mass on the certified action, (ii) Patch MCQ tests the checkpoint's choice between that action and alternatives rejected by the same verifier, and (iii) prefix-conditioned pass@$K$ evaluates support for functionally-correct generations and credits any continuation that the tests accept. Across ten pairs of public base and post-trained models, all three screens rank the cohort in close agreement with post-trained SWE-bench Verified pass@$1$. As our methods need only a benchmark's successful trajectories and its verifier, they can be applied to turn future agentic coding benchmarks into base-model evaluations.
2610.10478.paper_summary_zh: 如何預測哪個基礎檢查點值得進行昂貴的後訓練代理性回合？端到端的 pass@$K$ 測試是否成功行為已經出現在基礎模型的分佈中，但它對於代理性編碼來說並不適合：許多基礎檢查點無法可靠地產生完成任務所需的良好工具調用。單次或短期任務通過將多步互動簡化為固定提示和單一補丁來避免這些工具調用失敗，但它們迴避了我們所關心的核心能力：在多個使用工具的步驟中隨著資料庫的演變保持一致的狀態。為了彌補這一差距，我們將成功的後訓練代理軌跡視為基礎模型潛力的前瞻信號。在每個軌跡上重播並在每次代碼更改步驟後重新運行測試，以確定關鍵步驟：第一步的累積補丁使資料庫從失敗轉變為通過，證明所記錄的行動在先前的上下文中解決了任務。受到代理性痕跡的覆蓋原則的激勵，我們在這一步構建了三個篩選器，這些篩選器不需要基礎檢查點來從冷啟動驅動裝置：(i) 關鍵行動 BPB（每字節位數）測量經過認證的行動的概率質量，(ii) 補丁 MCQ 測試檢查點在該行動和同一驗證者拒絕的替代方案之間的選擇，以及 (iii) 前綴條件 pass@$K$ 評估對功能正確生成的支持，並對測試接受的任何延續給予信用。在十對公共基礎和後訓練模型中，所有三個篩選器在與後訓練 SWE-bench 驗證的 pass@$1$ 之間緊密一致地對該群體進行排名。由於我們的方法僅需要基準的成功軌跡及其驗證者，因此可以應用於將未來的代理性編碼基準轉化為基礎模型評估。
